title: Verification Gates
service: VerifyGate: a deterministic verification gate over lesson 33/36/37 artifacts (feedback records with argv commands, scope report, rule report with severities, coverage), HMAC-signed human overrides bound to task and HEAD, an append-only signed overrides.jsonl, one JSON report per task at outputs/verification/<task_id>.json, a streamed Markdown summary, and gating for stacked commits
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network and no LLM: overrides are signed with a fixed test secret, and Part 4's gate is a function the test supplies

parts.lesson_anchor: What the gate checks (all acceptance commands ran and exited zero, no null exit codes); Refuse without exception (only a human overrides a block, with override_reason and overridden_by, as a signed change); Signed override log (timestamp, finding code, reason, signing user, current HEAD commit; the runtime refuses an override without the signature); code/main.py _acceptance_findings, record_override, verify_signature; quiz Q6, Q9, Q10, Q12
planted_bugs: command_text turns an argv list into str(list), so a lesson 37 record never matches the contract's command and every acceptance command is reported missing; the failure shows in acceptance_findings, the cause is two calls down in commands.py (quiz Q9)
latest_run returns the first matching record, so an acceptance command that failed and then passed on a retry still reports acceptance.failed (quiz Q6, Q10)

make_override signs the five string fields and only then adds ts, so verify_signature, which covers every field but the signature, rejects a fresh override and apply_overrides drops it; the symptom is in apply_overrides, the cause in signing.py
apply_overrides does not compare head_commit, so an override recorded at an older HEAD still clears the finding
acceptance_findings calls latest_run once per acceptance command, and each call shlex.joins the whole log again: O(commands x records)
parts.timing_assert: 400 acceptance commands against an 8,400-record log under 0.1 s. Measured on this machine (Python 3.12): at load average about 5, the starter with the other four bugs fixed takes 1.66-1.82 s, a reversed scan that returns on the first match 1.61-1.68 s (the acceptance runs sit early in the log), one index built per call 7.3-8.1 ms; with eight extra busy processes 3.2-3.4 s and 8-45 ms; at load average about 12, 2.07-2.34 s, 2.2-4.2 s and 7.2-9.2 ms. Normalizing every record once into a list and scanning that list per command is still commands x records comparisons, 25-70 ms and up to 160 ms under load, so the test does not promise to let it through
parts.overfix_guard: argv joined with plain spaces on both sides makes ['pytest', '-k', 'card', 'and', 'not', 'slow', ...] the same command as -k 'card and not slow'; a pass that a later run broke must block; one override clears only its own finding code and leaves the list it was given alone; an override for another task, with a changed reason or ts, signed with another secret, or without a signature does nothing; verify_signature changed to skip ts is caught by a re-timed entry; a null exit cannot be overridden; a warn is not overridden; the last valid override of a code is reported, and another task's override of the same code later in the log does not hide it; a blank reason and an empty secret are refused; the reversed early-return scan stays slow

parts.lesson_anchor: Signed override log, not Slack threads: every override is a row in outputs/verification/overrides.jsonl, signed, git-tracked; the runtime refuses any override that lacks the signature; skill refusal rule: off-the-record overrides defeat the gate; code/main.py _sign (canonical JSON, HMAC-SHA256, 32 hex digits) and _load_override_secret (fail closed)
parts.storage: an append-only JSON-lines file, one json.dumps(entry) per line; each entry is exactly the six fields plus an HMAC-SHA256 signature over their canonical JSON (sort_keys, compact separators); the signature covers content, not how the line is spelled
parts.exactness: entries read back equal to what was appended, and their canonical signing bytes are identical: a float ts with 17 significant digits, an int ts, a reason with non-ASCII text, quotes, backslashes and a tab, a line another tool wrote with reversed keys, spaced separators and raw UTF-8; earlier bytes of the file are never rewritten, by any writer
traps: an empty secret accepted
the file opened with w, or a whole-file rewrite that re-serializes another tool's line
no newline, or indent=2, so line numbers drift
line numbers counted per instance, so two writers report (5, 5, 6)
append that does not check the entry, checks only the signature (a signed entry with an extra field), or writes before refusing
entries() that verifies the signature but not the fields, so a signed line with ts renamed to timestamp reads back
a line required to read exactly as json.dumps writes it
the empty piece after the last newline parsed as a line
0-based line numbers, a JSONDecodeError instead of LogTampered, blank lines skipped, a null line crashing
a field given twice accepted because Python keeps the last value
a non-ASCII signature handed to hmac.compare_digest (TypeError)
an int ts rewritten as a float, which changes the signed bytes
clarifying_questions: skip or raise on a bad line

parts.lesson_anchor: Deterministic, not probabilistic (same verdict for the same artifact set); One report, one path (outputs/verification/<task_id>.json); warn annotates, block prevents passed; Coverage floor as a first-class check (80% default, more than one point below the previous merge blocks); --strict promotes warns to blocks; lesson 33 severity tagging at write time; skill refusal rules (no acceptance command, missing rule report or feedback log fail closed); code/main.py _coverage_findings and its isclose boundary; quiz Q3, Q4, Q7, Q11, Q15
traps: every failed rule blocks as in the lesson code, or an unknown severity ('Warn', 'critical', missing) passed through or lower-cased instead of blocking
a missing artifact (None) counted as clean, an empty one counted as missing, or missing-artifact findings moved out of their source's place
no acceptance command treated as clean
strict promoting info, or not recorded in the verdict
overrides applied before strict, not applied, or an overridden finding still blocking

coverage: delta > 0.01 or >= 0.01 (0.85 -> 0.84 blocks), round(delta, 2) (0.85 -> 0.839 passes), int() points (0.8599 -> 0.849 passes), abs_tol as wide as the threshold, rel_tol against zero (float noise warns)
the given floor ignored, 80 or 0 accepted as a floor, or 1.0 refused
the lesson's verification_report_<id>.json name, unsorted keys, a timestamp, append mode
task id not checked, checked only for slashes or only at its start, or cleaned with Path(task_id).name
clarifying_questions: a rule without a known severity
a task id with a slash

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 3 (a Markdown summary in addition to JSON; which fields belong in it); What the gate checks: a warn finding annotates the verdict, a block finding prevents passed: true; Use It: pre-handoff hook and manual triage read the report while the agent works; lesson 37 records arrive one by one as commands finish
parts.wire_format: Markdown text: one summary per change, each yielded as one string; summaries separated by a blank line, ---, and a blank line (a thematic break, not a setext underline), no break before the first or after the last; decided by the test's exact summary text and chunk list
traps: sections in the order findings first appear, findings sorted inside a section, a section for a severity without findings, overridden rows without by and reason, strict missing from the head line, or PASSED only when there are no findings
no summary before the first record, or the first one sent only once a record has been read (an empty stream then gets none)
a summary for every record, only when PASSED and FAILED flip, only when the verdict or a section's count changes, or every summary compared with the first one
break and summary yielded as two chunks, --- right under the last line, no blank line before or after ---, a break before the first summary, or a break after every summary
not again once the same text went out earlier
the gate skipped for records that look unimportant
the whole stream read before the first change goes out
side check, with the order spelled out in the docstring: no escaping, only pipes escaped, the backslash not escaped or escaped last, or only the detail column escaped

parts.lesson_anchor: Coverage floor against the previous merge (for a stacked commit, the commit it sits on); overrides carry the current HEAD commit; Use It: CI step with merge protection refusing without passed: true; Defense-in-depth: the gate sits at the pre-merge layer
traps: every commit compared with main, the parent's baseline passed on instead of its coverage, back to main when the parent has no coverage report, or CI's own previous kept
CI's coverage report changed in place
result in the order given, breadth first, or siblings sorted by sha
a waiting parent not holding its children, a failed parent holding them, or artifacts from an older push used
blocked_by from the commit's own verdict only, or the nearest failure instead of the first
an override signed at the parent reaching the child (HEAD not compared)
strict or the coverage floor not passed on
an unknown parent taken for the base, commits that never reach the base dropped, a sha given twice kept once
clarifying_questions: a parent not in the list

deviations: Part 1: the suggested defects are kept (argv compared as str(list), every run counted instead of the latest, overrides not applied with a stale HEAD still in force, and the per-command scan). verify itself is Part 3's to write, so the override defects live in apply_overrides (head_commit not compared) and in make_override, which signs before ts is added: a fresh override then fails verification one call away from where it was made. Null exits count on the latest run of an acceptance command (quiz Q10), so a crash that a rerun replaced is history. The timing case is 400 commands against 8,400 records instead of 1,000 against 50,000, so the slow version stays under two seconds.

Part 2: append-only HMAC-signed JSON lines as assigned, one signature per entry and no hash chain (that is chapter 13 lesson 30's ledger). The U+2028 / splitlines trap and torn-tail recovery are left out because chapter 14 already uses them (lessons 01, 02, 05, 08, 14); a cut-off line is only detected and reported by line number. The suggested float and non-ASCII exactness is checked on the canonical signing bytes, with an int ts next to the float ones, and a duplicate-key line is added as the domain's own parser-differential trap.

Part 3: as suggested (four sources, strict, overrides, fixed order, one path, same bytes), with the isclose boundary kept in the provided coverage_findings. Info findings come from soft off-scope writes (lesson 36) and info-severity rules (lesson 33's severity tagging), which also gives the rule report its own trap. Fail-closed handling of missing artifacts and of a contract without acceptance commands comes from the lesson's skill refusal rules and quiz Q7/Q11. 'A null exit cannot be overridden' is a rule of apply_overrides, so it is tested in Part 1.

Part 4: Markdown as assigned. stream_summaries takes the gate as a function, and the test supplies a scripted one, so this part does not depend on Part 3. A change is anything that changes the summary text, not only PASSED and FAILED flipping. The break is a blank line, --- and a blank line, because --- right under the last paragraph line of a passing summary is a setext heading. The cell escaping and its order (the backslash first) are spelled out in render_summary's docstring, because escaping the escape character first is already a main trap elsewhere in chapter 14; the sample report still carries every escaped character, so escaping is checked on the side, and the part's own traps are the section layout, the summary before any record, a summary only on a change, and where the break goes.

Part 5: as suggested, with the baseline for a parent without a coverage report taken from what the parent was compared against, artifacts made at an older push treated as waiting like missing ones, and a fork in the stack. 'The child must wait for the parent's report' is the waiting status; the first blocker is reported per commit as blocked_by. Part 5 calls the real verify, so it needs Part 3; the overrides check there exercises Part 1's HEAD binding.
